fast.why: Monday is a day deeds are presented to Allah, and the Prophet ﷺ liked to be fasting when his deeds were presented. Make your niyyah on Sunday night, or before Zuhr on Monday if you haven't eaten.

blessing: The people who quietly help you: a colleague who covers, a parent who prays for you, a driver who stops. Thank one of them by name today, and say Alhamdulillah for them.

verse.text: Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.

hadith.text: Whoever is patient, Allah will make him patient. No one has been given a gift better and more vast than patience.

lesson.title: Adab and akhlaq part 3: thanking people
lesson.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: "He who does not thank people has not thanked Allah" (Abu Dawud 4811, Tirmidhi 1954). Gratitude to Allah and gratitude to the people He used to help you go together. A sincere "thank you", a dua for them ("jazakallahu khayran"), or a small kindness back all count. On a heavy day at work, this also lifts your own heart, because you start noticing the good around you.

quote.text: Don't be selfish and think only about yourself. Be sensitive to the needs of others. If you want people to respect your time, respect theirs.

videos.title: Omar Suleiman: When You Need to Feel Loved (Allah's Names, Ep. 10: kindness and appreciation)

name.text: He gives freely, with nothing owed: "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower" (3:8). Everything you have is a gift, so ask Him and thank Him.
"I am Ever-Forgiving to whoever repents, believes and does good" (20:82). Close the day with istighfar and put down today's mistakes.

quote.text: Almighty, We ask You to hide our faults, forgive our sins and protect us from all evil and harm in this world and the Hereafter. Aameen.

world.text: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists set it at 85 seconds to midnight on 27 Jan 2026, the closest ever, citing nuclear risk, AI and great-power rivalry.
Forecasters' chance of a 'World War Three' before 2050 (10M+ deaths, major powers involved).
Prof Jiang's latest lectures on geopolitics and where great-power conflict is heading.

Nuclear deterrence makes all-out war a losing move for every major power, so the stable outcome (flashing) is 'compete, don't fight': trade wars, arms races and proxy conflicts. The real danger is a misread in a crisis like Taiwan or Ukraine, which is why the clock and the forecast are rising. Meter: 2 of 5.
